title: Retire six writing rules into unplaceable-reference
summary: Six writing rules — bare-reference, reference-without-label, reference-without-link, chat-local-reference, undefined-name and undefined-name-at-start — are deleted and folded into the single unplaceable-reference rule, which now also carries the old link warning as a statistical, warning-level finding. Because those ids are gone, every surface that could still name one (suppressions, writing.levels, osf-expect declarations, osf explain, the OSF_WRITING_CHAT_LOCAL_LABELS env var and the writing.chat_local_labels config key) is taught to say the id is retired and name its replacement instead of failing silently or with a bare 'not a rule id'.

lanes.label: CLI surface
lanes.subtitle: osf binary
lanes.summary: The commands a user or agent invokes: lint, verify, explain, and the config loader that resolves osf.toml and the environment.

lanes.label: Lint core
lanes.subtitle: osf-lint-core crate
lanes.summary: The shared engine: expectation checking, suppression scanning and the human/SARIF renderers. It now knows about retired rule ids so it can point at replacements.

lanes.label: Writing rules
lanes.subtitle: osf::lints::writing
lanes.summary: The rule set itself. Six rules are gone; unplaceable-reference absorbs their coverage and gains the unlinked-reference warning.

lanes.label: Agent integrations
lanes.subtitle: dsh, omp, opencode
lanes.summary: Adapters that read osf's exit code and stderr/stdout and surface the rule id in a refusal reason. Only their fixtures changed.

nodes.label: osf CLI
nodes.subtitle: main.rs
nodes.summary: Entry point. `explain` now short-circuits on a retired rule id and prints the replacement instead of 'no such rule'; expectation findings gain a retired-rule variant.

nodes.label: Config loader
nodes.subtitle: config.rs
nodes.summary: Resolves osf.toml, env vars and flags into a Config. Drops chat_local_labels, notices the retired env var on stderr, rewrites the removed-key error, and rejects writing.levels entries naming a retired rule.

nodes.label: RETIRED_RULE_IDS
nodes.subtitle: &[(&str, &str)]
nodes.summary: The single table mapping each of the six deleted rule ids to unplaceable-reference. Every migration message in the change reads from it.

nodes.label: verify
nodes.subtitle: verify.rs
nodes.summary: Pre-commit and pre-push checks. Declared-fixture mismatches now also emit expectation-retired-rule findings naming the replacement.

nodes.label: expectation check
nodes.subtitle: check()
nodes.summary: Compares a fixture's declared rule ids against what actually fired. A declared id in the retired table is reported in its own `retired` bucket, and its replacement firing is not also reported as unexpected.

nodes.label: suppression engine
nodes.subtitle: apply_suppressions()
nodes.summary: Scans osf-disable markers and validates the rule ids they name. An id in the retired table still errors, but the message now says it was replaced and by what.

nodes.label: human / SARIF renderers
nodes.subtitle: human.rs, sarif.rs
nodes.summary: Unchanged in behaviour; their test fixtures were updated to the new rule id.

nodes.label: lint_writing
nodes.subtitle: writing/mod.rs
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the writing rules. No longer calls undefined_names, passes RETIRED_RULE_IDS into suppression, and resolves every finding's level from its own evidence rather than special-casing unplaceable-reference.

nodes.label: unplaceable-reference
nodes.subtitle: rules.rs
nodes.summary: The surviving rule. It now emits a warning-level, statistical finding for a labelled repo reference with no link, taking over what reference-without-link did, and keeps the error for anything genuinely unplaced.

nodes.label: six retired rules
nodes.subtitle: bare-reference, chat-local-reference, undefined-name, ...
nodes.summary: Deleted from SENTENCE_RULES, rule_ids and RULE_META. Their coverage is now unplaceable-reference's; their ids survive only in RETIRED_RULE_IDS so old references can be redirected.

nodes.label: WritingConfig
nodes.subtitle: chat_local_labels removed
nodes.summary: The chat_local_labels field and its default list are gone, along with the OSF_WRITING_CHAT_LOCAL_LABELS env mapping. chat_local_phrases and must_explain_names are the documented replacements.

nodes.label: dsh adapter
nodes.subtitle: integrations/dsh
nodes.summary: Reads osf's exit code and stderr into a refusal reason. Only its test fixture's rule id changed.

nodes.label: omp adapter
nodes.subtitle: integrations/omp
nodes.summary: Reads a decision-json block reason. Test and README examples updated to the new rule id.

nodes.label: opencode adapter
nodes.subtitle: integrations/opencode
nodes.summary: Same decision-json contract as omp; only the fixture rule id changed.

edges.label: load config
edges.summary: Every command resolves config first; the retired-key and retired-level rejections happen here.

edges.label: explain redirect
edges.summary: `osf explain bare-reference` now reads the retired table and prints the replacement instead of exiting 2 with 'no such rule'.

edges.label: reject retired levels
edges.summary: writing.levels keyed by a retired id is refused with a message naming unplaceable-reference.

edges.label: apply_suppressions(..., RETIRED_RULE_IDS)
edges.summary: The suppression engine now receives the retired table, so a marker naming a dead rule explains the migration instead of just rejecting the id.

edges.label: no longer runs
edges.summary: undefined_names and the sentence/chat-local rules are no longer invoked; their ids are absent from rule_ids().

edges.label: absorbs coverage
edges.summary: The surviving rule now covers what all six deleted rules caught, including the unlinked-reference warning.

flows.title: A stale rule id meets the new rule set
flows.summary: What happens when a repository still names one of the six deleted rules — in a suppression marker, a writing.levels entry, an osf-expect declaration, or an osf explain call — and the replacement rule fires instead.

messages.label: load osf.toml + env
messages.note: A writing.levels key naming a retired id is rejected here, before any linting runs.

messages.label: run rule
messages.note: The rule now also warns on a labelled repo reference with no link, the case reference-without-link used to own.

response.shape: Finding { rule: &'static str, level: Level, evidence: Evidence, excerpt: String }

messages.label: suppression-unknown-rule: 'bare-reference' is not a rule id any more; it was replaced by 'unplaceable-reference'
Mismatch { retired: [("bare-reference", "unplaceable-reference")] }
messages.note: The replacement firing is not also reported as unexpected; only genuinely unrelated ids land there.

views.title: Architecture overview
views.summary: The four surfaces the change touches: the CLI and its config loader, the shared lint core, the writing rule set, and the agent integrations that consume osf's output.

views.title: Writing rule set after the merge
views.summary: Inside the writing container: six rules are gone, unplaceable-reference absorbs their coverage, and the config field that fed one of them is removed.

views.title: Where a retired rule id is caught
views.summary: The four entry points that can still name a deleted rule id, and the single table they all read to name the replacement.
